systems.system: Rwanda Electronic Single Window System (Single Transaction Portal)

note: States only that appeals against Customs Management decisions are lodged through the electronic single window from 2026-03-01; says nothing of declarations or of other agencies joined to it.

facts.fact: The article says Rwanda introduced the ASYCUDA++ customs management system in 2004 and upgraded it to ASYCUDA World in 2012, halving customs clearance times, according to TradeMark East Africa.

note: Only names Rwanda as a Northern Corridor country; RECTS is cargo tracking, not clearance.

facts.fact: UNCTAD describes ASYCUDA World as Rwanda's system for processing international trade transactions.
UNCTAD says it will work with MINICOM and Rwanda Revenue Authority to optimize ASYCUDA World's selectivity/risk modules and activate import clearance.

note: Names RESW and a single window only in abbreviations and a control; states nothing on the status of customs processing.

facts.fact: TradeMark Africa reports that the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi are interconnected through the East African Community Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform, unveiled in revamped form on 27 January 2025.
facts.system: EAC Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform

note: Database record; the single window claim is already held.
